newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Poll will not effect Britain's HK policy - Patten.
newsitem.headline: Poll will not effect Britain's HK policy - Patten.

text.p: Britain's policy on Hong Kong will stay the same regardless of who wins Thursday's general election in the United Kingdom, former British cabinet minister and now Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday.

"Policy on Hong Kong has had cross-party support at Westminster," Patten told reporters. "I don't believe that will change for one moment, whatever happens in the ballot box in the United Kingdom tomorrow."

Patten said he based his view on the fact that he "kept in regular touch" with many players in British politics, including Prime Minister John Major and his ministers, Labour Party leader Tony Blair and Liberal Democrat Party chief Paddy Ashdown.
Patten, a former Conservative party chairman credited with engineering the Tories' unexpected victory in Britain's 1992 election, declined to comment on the outcome of Thursday's vote.
A Reuters poll of 20 British political experts on Wednesday showed that Labour is poised to sweep to a 92-seat majority.
Patten's career as Hong Kong's 28th and last governor ends at midnight on June 30 when Britain hands back its last major colony to China.
After the handover ceremony, Patten and Prince Charles will sail out of Hong Kong aboard the royal yacht Britannia.
